Aisha (ml): Quick sync — brought up a new quantized candidate (q4_0) in the eval harness and noticed ~8% drop vs fp16 on our judge-driven pairwise benchmark. Can we triage judge-related causes before assuming model degradation?
Ben (research): Good call. Could be judge sensitivity to quantization artifacts. Did you run the control where the judge evaluates two identical fp16 copies?
Aisha (ml): Yes. Control looks fine (0.8% noise). But when the candidate is quantized it flips more often. Also the runner produced a bunch of "tie" outcomes for several pairs today, which feels off.
Carlos (ml infra): I saw the runner logs. There's a bug where if the judge response is malformed (missing `preference`), the aggregator increments `ties` instead of retrying. I'll post the log snippet in a sec.
Diane (eval): That would explain both symptoms: malformed judge responses from q-outputs + aggregator treating them as ties. We should change logic to `retry_count` or mark as `invalid` and surface to triage.
Carlos (ml infra): Log snippet: ```
2026-03-20T15:12:07Z judge=redwood-judge-q temp=0.2 id=pair-342 resp=null -> agg:ties++
2026-03-20T15:12:07Z judge=redwood-judge-fp16 temp=0.2 id=pair-342 resp=choice:A -> agg:count[A]++
```
Ben (research): Two things to do: 1) fix runner to not conflate malformed with genuine ties; 2) revisit tie-breaker policy in rubric so tied counts don't mask judge bias.
Frank (applied): For tie-breaker, we've used simple majority, then "first-respondent wins" historically. That's brittle. Propose deterministic fallback: compute "consistency_score" per judge across repeat prompts, then on tie choose the judge with higher consistency, else fall back to an anchor judge ensemble.
Eve (security): Anchor/ensemble is fine but remember we must avoid amplifying systematic bias. If the anchor judges are skewed, fallback could worsen fairness. We need slice-aware metrics in the tie-break logic.
Diane (eval): Agreed. Suggest add these to rubric: 1) majority vote when clear, 2) if tie -> use judge_consistency (repeat 3x on same pair), 3) if still tied -> use a calibrated ensemble (3 judges) with weighted voting by calibrated reliability per slice. Record metadata: "tie_reason" and which path used.
Aisha (ml): That sounds good. For calibration, Ben, can you run a quick experiment to compute reliability per judge on the dev set slices? We need per-judge reliability on safety, factuality, and demographic slices.
Ben (research): On it. I'll produce a minimal pipeline: sample 1k pairs, run each judge 3x, compute agreement, entropy, and per-slice flip rate. Output CSV with columns: judge, slice, reliability_score, entropy_mean, flip_rate.
Carlos (ml infra): I'll patch the runner: (a) treat malformed responses as `invalid` and retry up to 2 times, (b) expose `invalid_count` in the aggregator output, (c) add a `tie_resolution` field in the result JSON with values {majority, consistency, ensemble, human_review}.
Frank (applied): Small note — add a CI check that the aggregator never silently increments ties by >1% without creating a ticket. We had silent regressions before.
ci-bot: Issue created: RED-ENG-ML-742 "aggregator: malformed responses treated as ties". CI alert posted in #eng-infra (link: https://redwood.atlassian/RED-ENG-ML-742).
Eve (security): Also add a requirement that ensemble judges used for fallback are from different model families/quantization configs to reduce correlated failure modes.
Diane (eval): Good point. We'll add a small test harness to the eval suite: generate adversarial anchors (prompt perturbations) and ensure fallback ensemble reduces flip_rate by >= 25% vs single judge baseline.
Aisha (ml): Timeline? Would love a patch + bench within this week so we can re-evaluate the q4_0 numbers before the release candidate.
Carlos (ml infra): Patch for runner today, CI test tomorrow.
Ben (research): I'll have the reliability CSV + short writeup by EOD tomorrow.
Frank (applied): I'll add the rubric text and a tiny GH PR template for human-review cases.
Diane (eval): I'll update the dashboard to show `invalid_count`, `tie_resolution`, and per-slice judge reliability. That should make it easier to spot judge-induced regressions.
Aisha (ml): Awesome. One more ask: can we add a surgical eval that isolates quantization-induced lexical artifacts (e.g., truncated tokens) vs actual reasoning failures? Might help us communicate to model-team.
Ben (research): Yep — I'll add a small set of diagnostic prompts (token-boundary stress tests) and include them in the reliability report.
Aisha (ml): Thanks all :pray: Let's regroup after the CI runs.
